title: The Lion Becomes the King of Beasts, part 1
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: After climbing down from the china wall the travelers found themselves in a disagreeable country, full of bogs and marshes and covered with tall, rank grass. It was difficult to walk without falling into muddy holes, for the grass was so thick that it hid them from sight. However, by carefully picking their way, they got safely along until they reached solid ground. But here the country seemed wilder than ever, and after a long and tiresome walk through the underbrush they entered another forest, where the trees were bigger and older than any they had ever seen.
“This forest is perfectly delightful,” declared the Lion, looking around him with joy. “Never have I seen a more beautiful place.”

“Not a bit of it,” answered the Lion. “I should like to live here all my life. See how soft the dried leaves are under your feet and how rich and green the moss is that clings to these old trees. Surely no wild beast could wish a pleasanter home.”
“Perhaps there are wild beasts in the forest now,” said Dorothy.
“I suppose there are,” returned the Lion, “but I do not see any of them about.”
They walked through the forest until it became too dark to go any farther. Dorothy and Toto and the Lion lay down to sleep, while the Woodman and the Scarecrow kept watch over them as usual.

When morning came, they started again. Before they had gone far they heard a low rumble, as of the growling of many wild animals. Toto whimpered a little, but none of the others was frightened, and they kept along the well-trodden path until they came to an opening in the wood, in which were gathered hundreds of beasts of every variety. There were tigers and elephants and bears and wolves and foxes and all the others in the natural history, and for a moment Dorothy was afraid. But the Lion explained that the animals were holding a meeting, and he judged by their snarling and growling that they were in great trouble.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the country beyond the china wall like?
options: Full of bogs and marshes and tall rank grass
A smooth white floor like a platter
Rich farmland with blue-painted fences
A stretch of sand with nothing growing

questions.prompt: Per the passage, why was walking difficult there?
options: The thick grass hid the muddy holes
The ground was covered in loose stones
The marsh water came up to their knees
The wind blew hard against them

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Lion say about the new forest?
options: That it was perfectly delightful
That it was gloomy and unpleasant
That he had lived there as a cub
That it hid too many dangers

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Scarecrow say about the forest?
options: That it seems gloomy
That it is full of wild beasts
That the trees may fight them again
That they should go around it

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did they hear the next morning?
options: A low rumble, like many animals growling
The ringing of a distant bell
The shouting of the Quadling people
The barking of a china dog

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Lion like the forest so much?
options: The soft leaves and green moss make a fine home for a beast
It reminds him of the Emerald City he has left
It has no other wild beasts living in it
The trees there cannot bend down their branches

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how did Toto react to the growling?
options: He whimpered a little
He barked loudly in reply
He ran ahead to investigate
He hid in Dorothy's basket

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what did the Lion judge from the snarling?
options: That the beasts were in great trouble
That they were hunting something nearby
That they had scented the travellers
That they were fighting among themselves

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does rank describe about the grass?
options: Coarse and overgrown
Neatly cut and short
Dry and brown with drought
Arranged in straight rows

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: A hard march ends in a forest the Lion loves and a gathering of beasts
A hard march ends with the party lost among the marshes
The Lion refuses to enter a forest full of wild beasts
The travellers are attacked by tigers and bears at once

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what were the trees of the new forest like?
options: Bigger and older than any they had seen
Small and thinly scattered
Made entirely of white china
The same fighting trees as before

questions.prompt: Per the passage, who kept watch while the others slept?
options: The Woodman and the Scarecrow
The Lion alone
Dorothy and Toto together
Nobody kept watch that night

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what kinds of beasts were in the opening?
options: Tigers, elephants, bears, wolves, and foxes
Only lions, gathered from the whole forest
Winged monkeys and field mice
Beasts made of china, like the country behind

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how did Dorothy feel at the sight of the beasts?
options: Afraid, for a moment
Delighted at the spectacle
Certain they meant no harm
Too tired to care at all

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what did the Lion answer about wild beasts?
options: That he supposes there are some, though he sees none
That the forest is certainly empty of them
That they will not come near a lion
That he will drive them all away

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does disagreeable describe?
options: Unpleasant country to travel through
Country too steep to climb
Country nobody has ever entered
Country full of quarrelling people

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: Rough country gives way to a forest where the beasts are holding council
A journey through marshes that ends with everyone lost
A quarrel between the Lion and the Scarecrow about the forest
An attack by wild beasts as soon as they enter the wood
